DeclaredKind.description:
A Plugin kind a Plugin implements, and the capabilities of it that the
Plugin claims: its kind's suite proves each, and a capability not
declared stays unproved.

capabilities.description: The capabilities it claims, as its kind's suite names them.

Download.description: A download the engine checks against its digest.

Grant.description:
A power a Plugin asks for in its manifest's `permissions`, beyond
domains and Secret references.

oneOf.description:
A Secret's value itself, rather than the engine inserting it on the
way out.
Causing Effects.
Running script in a page.
A logged-in Session's credentials.

HookStageName.description: A Hook stage's `snake_case` name: one of Collie's, or another Product's or a newer engine's, which a reader keeps as received.

oneOf.description: Before a main-frame navigation is sent.
Once a navigation's response arrived, before the engine's own page work.
At a navigation's `load`.
Once a Run started; observe-only.
Once a Checkpoint was taken; observe-only.
Once a Run moved to another Group member; observe-only.
Once a Limit was reached; observe-only.
Once a Run ended; observe-only.

Limits.description:
A process Plugin's resource limits per instance, ADR 0033's defaults
where the manifest is silent; Operator policy caps each.

concurrency.description: The calls it may hold at once: 4 by default.

cpu_time.description: The CPU time it may take, in seconds: an hour by default.

memory.description: The memory it may hold, in bytes: 256 MiB by default.

open_files.description: The files it may hold open at once: 128 by default.

processes.description: The processes it may run at once, itself included: 1 by default.

ManifestBrowser.description:
A browser a Plugin adds (ADR 0033), which the engine downloads, checks
and launches itself.

platforms.description: Its download for each platform, such as `linux-x64`.

ManifestModel.description:
A Model provider's model (ADR 0101), with its declared capabilities and
price.

id.description:
The model's ID, the part of a Model reference after the provider
name.

input_price.description: The price of a million input tokens, such as `3 USD`.

max_output_tokens.description: The most tokens one answer holds.

output_price.description: The price of a million output tokens, such as `15 USD`.

strategies.description: The structured output strategies it accepts, best first.

NetworkLevel.description:
What a process Plugin may reach on the network (ADR 0033), derived from
its kinds rather than chosen: see [`NetworkLevel::allowed_for`].

oneOf.description:
Nothing: it creates no socket, and reaches the outside only through
the engine's calls back.
TCP streams through the engine's proxy, to the hosts it may reach.
The network directly.

Permissions.description:
What a Plugin may do beyond its kinds' calls (ADR 0033), each held to
what Operator policy approved for it.

domains.description: The domains it may reach through the engine.

grants.description: What else it asks for, each granted or refused on its own.

PluginCancelParams.description:
What `$/cancel` names: the call the engine no longer awaits, whose late
result it refuses.

deadline.description: Whether the call passed its deadline, rather than being stopped.

PluginHelloParams.description:
What the starter of a Plugin says in its `hello`. A field a newer
starter adds is read as absent.

network_level.description: The network level the instance is confined to.

product.description: The Product whose executable runs the Plugin.

protocol.description: The plugin protocol versions the starter speaks.

PluginHelloResult.description:
What a Plugin answers to `hello`, which the engine holds to the approved
manifest.

hook_stages.description: The Hook stages it implements, for a Hook.

network_level.description: The network level it was built to run at.

protocol_version.description:
The plugin protocol version the Plugin speaks, the newest it shares
with the starter.

PluginKindName.description: A Plugin kind's `snake_case` name: one of Collie's, or another Product's or a newer engine's, which a reader keeps as received.

oneOf.description: A Hook, run at a fixed stage of a navigation, a page or a Run.
A Browser backend, which supplies a Session's browser.
An Extractor, which turns a page into its main content.
A Model provider, which answers model calls.
A Decision provider, which picks one of several options.
A Secret provider, which resolves the references of its scheme.
A Challenge solver.
A Proxy provider.
A Search provider.
A Code source, which reads a one-time code for a login.
A Notification channel.

browsers.description: The browsers it adds, each by download and digest per platform.

entrypoint.description:
What the engine starts: a script the runtime runs, or an executable
without one, by its path in the bundle.

env.description:
The variables of its environment, each by the setting of the Plugin
that values it; nothing is inherited, and no loader variable is
allowed.

files.description: The paths outside its bundle it may read.

hook_stages.description: The Hook stages it implements, for a Hook.

limits.description: Its resource limits, which Operator policy caps.

manifest_version.description: The version of the manifest format it is written in.

models.description:
For a Model provider, its models, each with its capabilities and
price (ADR 0101).

network_level.description: What it may reach on the network, which its kinds bound.

permissions.description: What it may do beyond its kinds' calls.

protocol.description: The plugin protocol versions it speaks.

provider_name.description:
For a Model provider, the provider name a Model reference names it
by (ADR 0101).

runtime.description:
The language runtime it runs on, which the engine provides from its
runtime cache.

scheme.description: For a Secret provider, the reference scheme it resolves (ADR 0092).

settings_schema.description:
The JSON Schema of its settings, which the engine validates them
against and the CLI and MCP take the fields of.

spend.description: Its spend outside the engine, by unit.

PluginPingParams.description: What `$/ping` says: nothing but the Trace context it may carry.

PluginPingResult.description: What a Plugin answers to `$/ping`: nothing.

PluginProtocolRange.description: A range of plugin protocol versions, both ends included.

Product.description:
One of Goodfetch's two Products (ADR 0084), by its mark as the catalog
writes it.

oneOf.description: Browser automation; Foxhound contains it.
Crawling, which contains Collie.

RequestId.description: A request's id, which its reply carries back.

RequestMeta.description:
What a request's `_meta` holds (ADR 0132), which its runtime writes and
never a program: its Trace context, with no Baggage, and the raw mark of
a call a program made through the raw `call` (ADR 0099). A closed
object: the engine refuses any other key. The schema checks only that
each Trace context field is a string: a receiver drops a value it cannot
use, and never fails the call for it.

raw.description:
Whether the program sent the call through the raw `call`, the way
down to an operation its SDK does not generate (ADR 0099): an SDK
sets it on that call alone, and refuses a `_meta` the program writes
into its params, so a program neither forges nor removes it. The
engine validates and enforces a raw call as any other.

traceparent.description:
The caller's span, as W3C Trace Context's `traceparent` header
holds it.

tracestate.description:
Its vendors' values, as W3C Trace Context's `tracestate` header
holds them.

RunId.description: A Run ID (ADR 0036): lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, never a name Windows reserves for a device.

Runtime.description: The language runtime a Plugin runs on.

oneOf.description: None: its entrypoint is an executable.
Node.js.
Python.

Spend.description: A unit of a Plugin's spend outside the engine (ADR 0033).

max_per_call.description:
The most of the unit one call spends, which the engine reserves
before the call.

price.description:
Its price, such as `0.002 USD`; without one, a currency Limit treats
the unit as unbounded and refuses the call.

StructuredOutputStrategy.description: A way a model gives structured output (ADR 0101).

oneOf.description: The provider's own schema support.
A forced tool call.
The schema in the prompt, with JSON repair.
